sectors.name: Banks
sectors.note: US uses XLF (Financials) for its longer history.

events.title: Nasdaq peaks
events.description: The Nasdaq Composite hits its all-time high of the dot-com era, above 5,000.

events.title: Barron's "Burning Up" on dot-com cash burn
events.description: Barron's publishes an analysis showing dozens of internet companies would run out of cash within a year.

events.title: Nasdaq falls ~10% in a day
events.description: After a hotter-than-expected CPI report, the Nasdaq suffers one of its largest one-day point drops.

events.title: US presidential election (Bush v. Gore, disputed)
events.description: The US presidential election ends without a clear winner, starting a five-week recount dispute.

events.title: Fed surprise inter-meeting rate cut
events.description: The Federal Reserve cuts the federal funds rate by 50 bp between scheduled meetings.

events.title: 9/11 attacks
events.description: Terrorist attacks on New York and Washington; US stock markets stay closed until September 17.

events.title: Enron files for bankruptcy
events.description: Enron files for Chapter 11, then the largest bankruptcy in US history, after an accounting scandal.

events.title: China joins the WTO
events.description: China formally becomes a member of the World Trade Organization.

events.title: WorldCom accounting fraud disclosed
events.description: WorldCom discloses that it improperly booked about $3.8 billion of expenses as capital spending.

events.title: Sarbanes-Oxley Act signed
events.description: President Bush signs the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, tightening corporate governance and audit rules.

events.title: Nasdaq bottoms
events.description: The Nasdaq Composite closes at its bear-market low, down nearly 78% from its peak.

events.title: US invades Iraq
events.description: US-led forces begin military operations in Iraq.

events.title: Shanghai sell-off spreads globally
events.description: Shanghai stocks fall about 9% in a day and the sell-off spreads to Europe and the US.

events.title: BNP Paribas freezes three funds
events.description: BNP Paribas suspends three funds exposed to US subprime mortgages, citing evaporated liquidity.

events.title: Bear Stearns rescued by JPMorgan
events.description: JPMorgan agrees to buy Bear Stearns for $2 a share with Federal Reserve backing.

events.title: Fannie Mae & Freddie Mac taken over
events.description: The US government places Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac into conservatorship.

events.title: Lehman Brothers bankruptcy
events.description: Lehman Brothers files for Chapter 11 after rescue talks fail over the weekend.

events.title: US House rejects TARP
events.description: The House of Representatives votes down the $700 billion bank rescue plan.

events.title: US presidential election (Obama)
events.description: Barack Obama wins the US presidential election in the middle of the financial crisis.

events.title: China announces 4-trillion-yuan stimulus
events.description: China's State Council unveils a 4-trillion-yuan fiscal stimulus package.

events.title: Fed announces QE1
events.description: The Fed announces purchases of agency debt and mortgage-backed securities (QE1).

events.title: Global equities bottom
events.description: The S&P 500 closes at its financial-crisis low of 676.

events.title: Greece revises its deficit sharply upward
events.description: Greece's new government says the budget deficit will be far higher than previously reported.

events.title: First Greek bailout agreed
events.description: Eurozone ministers and the IMF agree a €110 billion rescue for Greece.

events.title: S&P downgrades US credit rating
events.description: Standard & Poor's cuts the US sovereign rating from AAA to AA+ after the debt-ceiling standoff.

events.title: Draghi: "whatever it takes"
events.description: ECB President Mario Draghi pledges to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro.

official_sources.label: ECB — speech at the Global Investment Conference

events.title: ECB announces OMT
events.description: The ECB unveils Outright Monetary Transactions to buy bonds of stressed euro countries.

events.title: Taper tantrum (Bernanke testimony)
events.description: Bernanke tells Congress the Fed could slow bond purchases, sending yields sharply higher.

events.title: Russia authorizes force in Crimea
events.description: Russia's upper house authorizes the use of military force in Ukraine.

events.title: ECB introduces negative rates
events.description: The ECB becomes the first major central bank to set a negative deposit rate.

events.title: SNB scraps the franc cap
events.description: The Swiss National Bank abandons its EUR/CHF 1.20 floor; the franc surges.

events.title: Shanghai Composite peaks
events.description: The Shanghai Composite peaks above 5,100 after a margin-fuelled rally.

events.title: Greek bailout referendum
events.description: Greek voters reject the creditors' bailout terms by a wide margin.

events.title: Shanghai falls ~8.5%
events.description: The Shanghai Composite drops about 8.5%, its worst day since 2007.

events.title: PBoC devalues the yuan
events.description: The People's Bank of China cuts the yuan's reference rate by nearly 2% and changes its fixing method.

events.title: "Black Monday": China-led global sell-off
events.description: Chinese stocks fall over 8% and trigger a global sell-off; the Dow drops 1,000 points at the open.

events.title: Fed's first hike since 2006
events.description: The Fed raises rates for the first time in almost a decade.

events.title: China suspends circuit breaker after second halt
events.description: Chinese markets halt for the day within 30 minutes; regulators then scrap the new circuit breaker.

events.title: Brexit referendum
events.description: The UK votes to leave the European Union.

events.title: US presidential election (Trump)
events.description: Donald Trump wins the US presidential election against market expectations.

events.title: French presidential runoff (Macron)
events.description: Emmanuel Macron defeats Marine Le Pen in the French presidential runoff.

events.title: US steel & aluminum tariffs announced
events.description: President Trump announces tariffs of 25% on steel and 10% on aluminum imports.

events.title: First US tariffs on Chinese goods take effect
events.description: US tariffs on $34 billion of Chinese imports take effect; China retaliates.

events.title: US midterm elections
events.description: Democrats win the House while Republicans keep the Senate.

events.title: US escalates China tariffs
events.description: President Trump says tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese goods will rise to 25%.

events.title: Attack on Saudi Abqaiq oil facility
events.description: Drone and missile strikes knock out about half of Saudi Arabia's oil output.

events.title: Wuhan reports pneumonia cluster to WHO
events.description: Chinese authorities report a cluster of pneumonia cases of unknown cause in Wuhan.

events.title: US kills Soleimani
events.description: A US strike in Baghdad kills Iranian general Qassem Soleimani.

events.title: US–China Phase One deal signed
events.description: The US and China sign the Phase One trade agreement.

events.title: Wuhan lockdown
events.description: China locks down Wuhan, a city of 11 million, to contain the new coronavirus.

events.title: Italy quarantines northern towns
events.description: Italy seals off towns in Lombardy and Veneto as Europe's first major outbreak emerges.

events.title: WHO declares a pandemic
events.description: The World Health Organization characterizes COVID-19 as a pandemic.

events.title: Fed cuts rates to zero
events.description: In an emergency Sunday move the Fed cuts rates to 0–0.25% and restarts asset purchases.

events.title: Fed announces unlimited QE; market bottom
events.description: The Fed commits to open-ended asset purchases and new credit facilities; US stocks bottom that day.

events.title: US presidential election (Biden)
events.description: The US presidential election goes to a days-long count; Joe Biden is projected the winner on November 7.

events.title: Pfizer announces vaccine efficacy
events.description: Pfizer and BioNTech report their vaccine is more than 90% effective in a late-stage trial.

events.title: US CPI jumps to 4.2%
events.description: US consumer prices rise 4.2% year over year, the fastest pace since 2008.

events.title: Powell retires "transitory"
events.description: Fed Chair Powell tells Congress it is time to retire the word "transitory" for inflation.

events.title: Russia invades Ukraine
events.description: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

events.title: Fed's first hike of the cycle
events.description: The Fed raises rates by 25 bp, its first hike since 2018.

events.title: Fed hikes 75 bp
events.description: The Fed raises rates by 75 bp, its largest hike since 1994.

events.title: ECB's first hike in 11 years
events.description: The ECB raises rates by 50 bp, ending eight years of negative rates.

events.title: UK "mini-budget" gilt crisis
events.description: Unfunded UK tax cuts trigger a collapse in gilts and sterling, forcing Bank of England intervention.

events.title: US chip export controls on China
events.description: The US restricts exports of advanced chips and chipmaking equipment to China.

events.title: US midterm elections
events.description: Republicans narrowly win the House; the expected "red wave" does not materialize.

events.title: ChatGPT launches
events.description: OpenAI releases ChatGPT to the public as a free research preview.

events.title: Silicon Valley Bank collapses
events.description: Regulators close Silicon Valley Bank after a deposit run, the largest US bank failure since 2008.

events.title: UBS takes over Credit Suisse
events.description: UBS agrees a government-brokered takeover of Credit Suisse; AT1 bonds are written off.

events.title: Nvidia's guidance blowout
events.description: Nvidia forecasts quarterly revenue far above expectations on demand for AI chips.

events.title: China restricts gallium & germanium exports
events.description: China announces export licensing for gallium and germanium, metals used in chips.

events.title: Hamas attack on Israel
events.description: Hamas launches a large-scale attack on Israel, starting the Gaza war.

events.title: US expands chip export controls
events.description: The US Commerce Department tightens restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China.

events.title: EU Parliament elections; Macron dissolves Assembly
events.description: Far-right gains in the EU elections lead Macron to call a snap French legislative election.

events.title: Nvidia becomes the world's most valuable company
events.description: Nvidia overtakes Microsoft as the world's most valuable listed company.

events.title: Yen carry-trade unwind
events.description: Japan's Nikkei falls 12% as yen-funded carry trades unwind, hitting global markets.

events.title: Fed's first cut of the cycle (50 bp)
events.description: The Fed starts its easing cycle with a 50 bp cut.

events.title: US presidential election (Trump)
events.description: Donald Trump wins a second term as US president.

events.title: DeepSeek sell-off
events.description: A low-cost Chinese AI model from DeepSeek prompts a sell-off in AI and chip stocks.

events.title: German federal election
events.description: The CDU/CSU led by Friedrich Merz wins Germany's federal election.

events.title: "Liberation Day" tariffs
events.description: President Trump announces sweeping "reciprocal" tariffs on most US trading partners.

events.title: 90-day tariff pause
events.description: The US pauses most reciprocal tariffs for 90 days while raising tariffs on China.

events.title: Israel strikes Iran
events.description: Israel launches strikes on Iranian nuclear and military sites.

events.title: China expands rare-earth export controls
events.description: China broadens export controls on rare earths and related technologies.

events.title: Nvidia reaches a $5T market cap
events.description: Nvidia becomes the first company to reach a $5 trillion market value.

events.title: US midterm elections
events.description: US midterm elections for Congress.
